title: Atol CD's Alfresco, Maarch and OnlyOffice stack moves documents without recording the decisions taken on them
content:
Atol CD delivers Alfresco, Maarch Courrier and OnlyOffice — a document stack. Together these systems move documents through an organisation and each keeps its own view of where a document currently sits, which is what a document-flow tool is for.

What none of them keeps is a decision record. The distinction is between a document's journey and the acts performed along it: a document system can show that a file reached a department and that a response exists, without asserting that an official decided something, on what authority, at what moment. The trail describes movement, and audit asks about judgement.

The research labels this the same Alfresco gap identified elsewhere in the corpus, the difference being the delivery base — French public-sector clients. That repetition is the useful part: the gap belongs to the document-management category rather than to one firm, so an argument constructed once transfers across the Alfresco leads, while the French public-sector footprint decides where it is worth making first.
